born.why: The code prioritizes starvation survival by eating novel fruits at extreme hunger (>95% or >80% with no safety record), uses tasting to build a safety database for specific fruit keys, and avoids known poisonous species to maximize long-term lifespan.

The code prioritizes starvation, uses a ratio of safe vs. bad experiences to assess risk (avoiding fruits with more bad than twice the good), tastes known fruits to confirm safety before storing, and carries novel fruits only when hunger is moderate to allow for later verification, balancing exploration with survival.

This code prioritizes survival by overriding all logic when hunger is critical, distinguishes between safe/known and unknown fruits based on diary history, and limits tasting of unknown fruits to necessary moments (high hunger or specific targets) to minimize the risk of poisoning.

The code prioritizes carrying known-safe fruits to build a pantry buffer against starvation, while tasting novel foods only when hunger is significant enough to justify the risk, ensuring efficient learning and survival.

The code improves survival by using trait-based generalization to identify poisonous fruits even when the species key is new, dynamically adjusts risk-taking based on hunger levels, and prioritizes carrying safe food for later use while only eating novel foods when necessary or when traits suggest safety.
